1e87509d-95fe-5804-a94b-d42ada81e4f7.title: Swapping the Order of Integration in a Triple Integral

e-11675.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Repeated Integral as a Mixed Integral
e-11675.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/a8d3e8c54d61326d9f7d5203d32bd48006c404e9d3990820cb8884c08df8dba3.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
\displaystyle
\int_0^1 \int_0^{2} \int_0^{\sqrt[3]{z}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $z,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xy$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
e-11675.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration $u_1(x,y)$ and $u_2(x,y)$ such that

$$
\int_0^1 \int_0^{2} \int_0^{\sqrt[3]{z}}  f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z
=
\iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\right] \textrm{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R = \big\{
(x,y,z) \:\: {:} \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt[3]{z} 
\big\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type I region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $z$-axis and in the direction of increasing $z,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/efc1013a8202f8eea26250b904cf3d4672b30d478ddaad72b6347b274bd33f7d.png)

The arrow enters the region through the bottom boundary and leaves through the top boundary:

- The bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x,y),$ is

$$
y = \sqrt[3]{z}, \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
z = y^3.
$$

- The top boundary of the region is $z = 1.$

Therefore, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R = \big\{
(x,y,z) \:\: {:} \:\: (x,y) \in D, \:\: y^3\leq z \leq 1
\big\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/3ae61409e70d4d6d6227a306ab1651331d9b40633248fd525cefbab519202a52.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $z$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\int_0^1 \int_0^{2} \int_0^{\sqrt[3]{z}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z
=
\iint\limits_D \left[\int_{y^3}^{1} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\right] \textrm{d}A.
$$

e-11676.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration in a Triple Integral
e-11676.problem:
Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
\displaystyle
\int_0^{1} \int_0^{1} \int_0^{1-z^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
e-11676.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration $u_1(x,y),$ $u_2(x,y),$ $v_1(x),$ $v_2(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
\int_0^{1} \int_0^{1} \int_0^{1-z^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x
=
\int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 1-z^2 \right\}
$$

Now, let's sketch the region. Since it is a type III region, we first draw the projection onto the $xz$-plane, given by

$$
E = \left\{
(x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1
\right\}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/8007b0f7348f9855a009aff56c676122a739e6210d4f024c524e72e3cfa23312.png)

Then, the region $R$ is shown in the diagram below, where $0 \leq y \leq  1-z^2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/97d0f5fc56498e1a044dbbfc07da571c1806903822dfdb1d68f877723ce9a559.png)

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x$ to $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type I region and its projection $D$ onto the $xy$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $z$-axis and in the direction of increasing $z,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/f5fab194951b50a2a0c81aff8d422b98be5145bbef3123ea746b86bcebd1e778.png)

The arrow enters the region through the bottom boundary and leaves through the top boundary:

- The top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x,y),$ is

$$
y = 1-z^2
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
z = \sqrt{1- y}.
$$

- The bottom boundary of the region is $z=0.$

Therefore, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,y) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq \sqrt{1-y} \big\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/403675d42fae7e437e62bcb3e254e3f7cf3997556606ed529807d83253d1c439.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xy$-plane with the top curve given by $y=1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/1e1fbae22c5ad39225a5de4e3c3aeb025cb41b21bbf0c127da57e3ada10c3087.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 1 \right\}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ then $x,$ we obtain

$$
\int_0^{1} \int_0^{1} \int_0^{1-z^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x
=
\int_0^{1} \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{0}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\sqrt{1-y}}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/63118a7b3d7fd589513f41ae1e721baf25305f480e683c984088fedb9a8d759b.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then over a region $D$ in the $yz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫02∫01−x2f(x,y,z)dydzdx so that it is integrated first with respect to x, then over a region D in the yz-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∬D[∫0yf(x,y,z)dx]dA
b
 ∬D[∫1−y21f(x,y,z)dx]dA
c
 ∬D[∫01−y2f(x,y,z)dx]dA
d
 ∬D[∫y1−y2f(x,y,z)dx]dA

Submit

decision.explanation: The region satisfies x≥0, y≥0, x²+y²≤1, and 0≤z≤2. For fixed (y,z), this gives 0≤x≤√(1−y²), with D={(y,z):0≤y≤1, 0≤z≤2}. Thus option c is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/63118a7b3d7fd589513f41ae1e721baf25305f480e683c984088fedb9a8d759b.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then over a region $D$ in the $yz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(y,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,\,:\,\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type II region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $x$-axis and in the direction of increasing $x,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7dbabd349afb41c00c447ab61e28139cc7818a74c54bd17a61eb77d05ae558ae.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y,z),$ is

$$
y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is $x=0.$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,\,:\,\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/4040e2d2eadc5c39b9224b1b39980de486fe6dd69dad1e63179c6cffcb4046b4.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $x$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

Question 1
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫02∫01−x2f(x,y,z)dydzdx so that it is integrated first with respect to x, then over a region D in the yz-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∬D[∫0yf(x,y,z)dx]dA
b
 ∬D[∫1−y21f(x,y,z)dx]dA
c
 ∬D[∫01−y2f(x,y,z)dx]dA
d
 ∬D[∫y1−y2f(x,y,z)dx]dA
e
 ∬D[∫yy2f(x,y,z)dx]dA
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration u1(y,z) and u2(y,z) such that

∫01∫02∫01−x2f(x,y,z)dydzdx=∬D[∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dx]dA.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type III region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,0≤z≤2,0≤y≤1−x2}

To change the order of integration from dydzdx to dxdA, we write R as a type II region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the x-axis and in the direction of increasing x, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

  • The front boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y,z), is y=1−x2⟹x=1−y2.

  • The back boundary of the region is x=0.

Therefore, the type II representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(y,z)∈D,0≤x≤1−y2},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to x and then over D, we obtain

∫01∫02∫01−x2f(x,y,z)dydzdx=∬D[∫01−y2f(x,y,z)dx]dA.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/63118a7b3d7fd589513f41ae1e721baf25305f480e683c984088fedb9a8d759b.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then over a region $D$ in the $yz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(y,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,\,:\,\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type II region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $x$-axis and in the direction of increasing $x,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7dbabd349afb41c00c447ab61e28139cc7818a74c54bd17a61eb77d05ae558ae.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y,z),$ is

$$
y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is $x=0.$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,\,:\,\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/4040e2d2eadc5c39b9224b1b39980de486fe6dd69dad1e63179c6cffcb4046b4.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $x$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

Question 2
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫04∫01−x/4∫01−x/4−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx so that it is integrated first with respect to z, then over a region D in the xy-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a
∬D[∫11−x/4−yf(x,y,z)dz]dA
b
∬D[∫01−yf(x,y,z)dz]dA
c
∬D[∫01+4xf(x,y,z)dz]dA
d
∬D[∫11+4xf(x,y,z)dz]dA
e
∬D[∫01−x/4−yf(x,y,z)dz]dA
Submit

decision.explanation: The region is bounded by x,y,z≥0 and x/4+y+z≤1. For fixed (x,y), the z limits are 0≤z≤1−x/4−y, over D={(x,y):0≤x≤4, 0≤y≤1−x/4}. Therefore option e gives the required order.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/9f4f24dd100758466d8a06eee113bada8b1bede4b48c0a3e694e4c1e3f1c2371.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $z,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xy$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(y,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{x}{4},\,\,0\le y\le 1-\frac{x}{4}-z}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type I region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $z$-axis and in the direction of increasing $z,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/dc1a9b6371456f635cd4b73fe99301fa349ceeec1341b9bd3b86f6bcd7ad8ba2.png)

The arrow enters the region through the bottom boundary and leaves through the top boundary:

- The top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x,y),$ is

$$
y=1-\frac{x}{4}-z\,⟹\,z=1-\frac{x}{4}-y.
$$

- The bottom boundary of the region is

$$
z=0.
$$

Therefore, the type I representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{x}{4}-y},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/07c4ee04dfba186348b3bd56b182477cec9ca1a581e37bb0eb4ab9a3d64ee515.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $z$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-y}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫04∫01−x/4∫01−x/4−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx so that it is integrated first with respect to z, then over a region D in the xy-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a
∬D[∫11−x/4−yf(x,y,z)dz]dA
b
∬D[∫01−yf(x,y,z)dz]dA
c
∬D[∫01+4xf(x,y,z)dz]dA
d
∬D[∫11+4xf(x,y,z)dz]dA
e
∬D[∫01−x/4−yf(x,y,z)dz]dA
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration u1(y,z) and u2(y,z) such that

∫04∫01−x/4∫01−x/4−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx=∬D[∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dz]dA.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type III region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤4,0≤z≤1−x4,0≤y≤1−x4−z}

To change the order of integration from dydzdx to dzdA, we write R as a type I region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the z-axis and in the direction of increasing z, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the bottom boundary and leaves through the top boundary:

  • The top boundary of the region, written in the form z=z(x,y), is y=1−x4−z⟹z=1−x4−y.

  • The bottom boundary of the region is z=0.

Therefore, the type I representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(x,y)∈D,0≤z≤1−x4−y},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to z and then over D, we obtain

∫04∫01−x/4∫01−x/4−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx=∬D[∫01−x/4−yf(x,y,z)dz]dA.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Repeated Integral as a Mixed Integral
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/9f4f24dd100758466d8a06eee113bada8b1bede4b48c0a3e694e4c1e3f1c2371.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $z,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xy$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(y,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{x}{4},\,\,0\le y\le 1-\frac{x}{4}-z}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type I region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $z$-axis and in the direction of increasing $z,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/dc1a9b6371456f635cd4b73fe99301fa349ceeec1341b9bd3b86f6bcd7ad8ba2.png)

The arrow enters the region through the bottom boundary and leaves through the top boundary:

- The top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x,y),$ is

$$
y=1-\frac{x}{4}-z\,⟹\,z=1-\frac{x}{4}-y.
$$

- The bottom boundary of the region is

$$
z=0.
$$

Therefore, the type I representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{x}{4}-y},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/07c4ee04dfba186348b3bd56b182477cec9ca1a581e37bb0eb4ab9a3d64ee515.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $z$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4}{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x/4-y}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

a

b

c

decision.explanation: The region satisfies x,y,z≥0 and x+2y+z≤2. Solving for y gives 0≤y≤(2−x−z)/2, over D={(x,z):0≤x≤2, 0≤z≤2−x}. Therefore option a is correct.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/96b24f85c19f388c152dae265c3794179ebc9e1e6fc06a1fe10f82627b73d29c.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{(2-x)/2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x-2y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(x,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{(2-x)/2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x-2y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{2-x}{2},\,\,0\le z\le 2-x-2y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type III region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/f08e4fc4d1d2933e9c12fe7df96a1029d66a83c68beff4fa31928cc010554766.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
z=2-x-2y\,⟹\,y=(2-x-z)/2.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{2-x-z}{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2639dbff9d1d4269abb59ccd3eefa0b246c8d1f183fd8f6ef132a41cc07e345d.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}{\int }_{0}^{2-x-2y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{(2-x-z)/2}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫02∫0(2−x)/2∫02−x−2yf(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then over a region D in the xz-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a

b
∬D[∫2−z(2−x−z)/2f(x,y,z)dy]dA
c
∬D[∫02−x−2zf(x,y,z)dy]dA

e
∬D[∫02−x−zf(x,y,z)dy]dA
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration u1(x,z) and u2(x,z) such that

∫02∫0(2−x)/2∫02−x−2yf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∬D[∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dy]dA.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤2,0≤y≤2−x2,0≤z≤2−x−2y}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dydA, we write R as a type III region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the y-axis and in the direction of increasing y, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

  • The front boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x,z), is z=2−x−2y⟹y=(2−x−z)/2.

  • The back boundary of the region is y=0.

Therefore, the type III representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,0≤y≤2−x−z2},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to y and then over D, we obtain

∫02∫02−x∫02−x−2yf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∬D[∫0(2−x−z)/2f(x,y,z)dy]dA.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Repeated Integral as a Mixed Integral
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/96b24f85c19f388c152dae265c3794179ebc9e1e6fc06a1fe10f82627b73d29c.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{(2-x)/2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x-2y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(x,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{(2-x)/2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x-2y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{2-x}{2},\,\,0\le z\le 2-x-2y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type III region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/f08e4fc4d1d2933e9c12fe7df96a1029d66a83c68beff4fa31928cc010554766.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
z=2-x-2y\,⟹\,y=(2-x-z)/2.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{2-x-z}{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2639dbff9d1d4269abb59ccd3eefa0b246c8d1f183fd8f6ef132a41cc07e345d.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}{\int }_{0}^{2-x-2y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{(2-x-z)/2}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

a

b
∬D[∫0z2f(x,y,z)dy]dA
c
∬D[∫1zf(x,y,z)dy]dA
d

decision.explanation: Since 0≤y≤1, the inequality z≤(y−1)²=(1−y)² implies √z≤1−y. Thus 0≤y≤1−√z, over D={(x,z):0≤x≤2, 0≤z≤1}. Option d is correct.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/d76d928d43054c7d5c026cc25b95fb55855c7a8cbdb5fb35b5ae1f1d39a35c90.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(x,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le (y-1)^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type III region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/116ae6061410bca820b3c89869b23a36b5cef47e4fe483e390ee43d1e52ff726.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
z=(y-1)^{2}\,⟹\,y=1-\sqrt{z}.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 1-\sqrt{z}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/5613cb5b9718914e35f7259e3fe9dfd69ce128a861d19995e2c836c2b76d0f58.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1-\sqrt{z}}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫02∫01∫0(y−1)2f(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then over a region D in the xz-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a
∬D[∫11−z2f(x,y,z)dy]dA
b
∬D[∫0z2f(x,y,z)dy]dA
c
∬D[∫1zf(x,y,z)dy]dA
d
∬D[∫01−zf(x,y,z)dy]dA
e
∬D[∫z−11f(x,y,z)dy]dA
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration u1(x,z) and u2(x,z) such that

∫02∫01∫0(y−1)2f(x,y,z)dzdydx=∬D[∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dy]dA.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤2,0≤y≤1,0≤z≤(y−1)2}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dydA, we write R as a type III region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the y-axis and in the direction of increasing y, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

  • The front boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x,z), is z=(y−1)2⟹y=1−z.

  • The back boundary of the region is y=0.

Therefore, the type III representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,0≤y≤1−z},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to y and then over D, we obtain

∫02∫01∫0(y−1)2f(x,y,z)dzdydx=∬D[∫01−zf(x,y,z)dy]dA.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option d. Since 0≤y≤1, z≤(y−1)² implies √z≤1−y, so 0≤y≤1−√z. The projection is D={(x,z):0≤x≤2, 0≤z≤1}. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option a.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Repeated Integral as a Mixed Integral
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/d76d928d43054c7d5c026cc25b95fb55855c7a8cbdb5fb35b5ae1f1d39a35c90.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(x,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le (y-1)^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type III region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/116ae6061410bca820b3c89869b23a36b5cef47e4fe483e390ee43d1e52ff726.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
z=(y-1)^{2}\,⟹\,y=1-\sqrt{z}.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 1-\sqrt{z}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/5613cb5b9718914e35f7259e3fe9dfd69ce128a861d19995e2c836c2b76d0f58.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1-\sqrt{z}}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 5
before.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/bd69636822b7a3f68805273a4ffd72c7011a4f945a3ebbac8dcd99191e7ea730.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{(3-x)/3}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-3y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then over a region $D$ in the $yz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.

Question 5
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫03∫0(3−x)/3∫03−x−3yf(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to x, then over a region D in the yz-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a
∬D[∫03−y+zf(x,y,z)dx]dA
b
∬D[∫33−3y−zf(x,y,z)dx]dA
c
∬D[∫0(y−z)/3f(x,y,z)dx]dA
d
∬D[∫33−y+zf(x,y,z)dx]dA
e
∬D[∫03−3y−zf(x,y,z)dx]dA
Submit

decision.explanation: The region satisfies x,y,z≥0 and x+3y+z≤3. For fixed (y,z), this gives 0≤x≤3−3y−z, over D={(y,z):0≤y≤1, 0≤z≤3−3y}. Thus option e is correct.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/bd69636822b7a3f68805273a4ffd72c7011a4f945a3ebbac8dcd99191e7ea730.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{(3-x)/3}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-3y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then over a region $D$ in the $yz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(y,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{(3-x)/3}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-3y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{3-x}{3},\,\,0\le z\le 3-x-3y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type II region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $x$-axis and in the direction of increasing $x,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/d26a7cc2c643b300226136a223be0fdebed4e17c99c2e562d1cc209caa023ea5.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y,z),$ is

$$
z=3-x-3y\,⟹\,x=3-3y-z.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is

$$
x=0.
$$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 3-3y-z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/5641e6fc83054a355a2010084e1c8be2cd2d8144eae2aad0706704247f03b258.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $x$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{(3-x)/3}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-3y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{3-3y-z}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫03∫0(3−x)/3∫03−x−3yf(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to x, then over a region D in the yz-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a
∬D[∫03−y+zf(x,y,z)dx]dA
b
∬D[∫33−3y−zf(x,y,z)dx]dA
c
∬D[∫0(y−z)/3f(x,y,z)dx]dA
d
∬D[∫33−y+zf(x,y,z)dx]dA
e
∬D[∫03−3y−zf(x,y,z)dx]dA
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration u1(y,z) and u2(y,z) such that

∫03∫0(3−x)/3∫03−x−3yf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∬D[∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dx]dA.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤3,0≤y≤3−x3,0≤z≤3−x−3y}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dxdA, we write R as a type II region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the x-axis and in the direction of increasing x, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

  • The front boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y,z), is z=3−x−3y⟹x=3−3y−z.

  • The back boundary of the region is x=0.

Therefore, the type II representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(y,z)∈D,0≤x≤3−3y−z},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to x and then over D, we obtain

∫03∫0(3−x)/3∫03−x−3yf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∬D[∫03−3y−zf(x,y,z)dx]dA.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Repeated Integral as a Mixed Integral
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/bd69636822b7a3f68805273a4ffd72c7011a4f945a3ebbac8dcd99191e7ea730.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{(3-x)/3}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-3y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then over a region $D$ in the $yz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(y,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{(3-x)/3}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-3y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{3-x}{3},\,\,0\le z\le 3-x-3y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type II region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $x$-axis and in the direction of increasing $x,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/d26a7cc2c643b300226136a223be0fdebed4e17c99c2e562d1cc209caa023ea5.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y,z),$ is

$$
z=3-x-3y\,⟹\,x=3-3y-z.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is

$$
x=0.
$$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 3-3y-z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/5641e6fc83054a355a2010084e1c8be2cd2d8144eae2aad0706704247f03b258.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $x$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{(3-x)/3}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-3y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{3-3y-z}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫x1∫01−yf(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then z, and then x. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∫01∫01−x∫0zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
b
 ∫01∫01−x∫x1−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
c
 ∫01∫01∫xzf(x,y,z)dydzdx
d
 ∫01∫0x∫01−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
e

Submit

decision.explanation: The original bounds require 0≤x≤1, y≥x, z≥0, and y+z≤1. For fixed x, this gives 0≤z≤1−x and x≤y≤1−z. Thus option b has the required order dy dz dx.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7094d1527f7feb9dac54cbd90e595dcbb71c11d5c0a32d1371c3c63c54127899.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/c48de52085373361c4e4de3010ebe36c1da702f0efec45b455dff891869086f2.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
z=1-y\,⟹\,y=1-z.
$$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,x\le y\le 1-z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/fd5d71a6d6509851e5131fe458b9672d59eb7ff6c07499949ae199b45f4ddae0.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane with the top curve given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=1-z \\ y=x\end{aligned}\,⟹\,x=1-z\,⟹\,z=1-x.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/12743c492a7f7883a2ecd8d3ca73138a324a53040cb8936f4794f9e8d84c8fd5.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-x}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{\int }_{x}^{1-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 6
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫x1∫01−yf(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then z, and then x. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∫01∫01−x∫0zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
b
 ∫01∫01−x∫x1−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
c
 ∫01∫01∫xzf(x,y,z)dydzdx
d
 ∫01∫0x∫01−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx
e
 ∫01∫0x∫z1−xf(x,y,z)dydzdx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find limits of integration u1(x,z), u2(x,z), v1(x), v2(x), a, and b such that

∫01∫x1∫01−yf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dydzdx.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,x≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dydzdx, we write R as a type III region and its projection D onto the xz-plane as a type I plane region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the y-axis and in the direction of increasing y, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

  • The left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x,z), is x=y⟹y=x

  • The right boundary of the region is z=1−y⟹y=1−z.

Therefore, the type II representation of R is R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,x≤y≤1−z}, as shown in the diagram below.

Now, we consider the projection D as a type I plane region in the xz-plane with the top curve given by {y=1−zy=x⟹x=1−z⟹z=1−x.

Hence, we have that D={(x,z):0≤x≤1,0≤z≤1−x}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then z, and then x, we obtain

∫01∫x1∫01−yf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∫01∫01−x∫x1−zf(x,y,z)dydzdx.

content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7094d1527f7feb9dac54cbd90e595dcbb71c11d5c0a32d1371c3c63c54127899.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/c48de52085373361c4e4de3010ebe36c1da702f0efec45b455dff891869086f2.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
z=1-y\,⟹\,y=1-z.
$$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,x\le y\le 1-z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/fd5d71a6d6509851e5131fe458b9672d59eb7ff6c07499949ae199b45f4ddae0.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xz$-plane with the top curve given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=1-z \\ y=x\end{aligned}\,⟹\,x=1-z\,⟹\,z=1-x.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/12743c492a7f7883a2ecd8d3ca73138a324a53040cb8936f4794f9e8d84c8fd5.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-x}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{\int }_{x}^{1-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 7
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫02∫0y2f(x,y,z)dxdydz. so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then x, and then z. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∫01∫02∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
b
 ∫01∫0x∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
c
 ∫01∫02∫x2xf(x,y,z)dydxdz
d
 ∫01∫0x∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
e
 ∫01∫01∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
Submit

decision.explanation: The original region has 0≤z≤1, 0≤y≤√2, and 0≤x≤y². Since y≥0, x≤y² is equivalent to y≥√x. Therefore 0≤x≤2 and √x≤y≤√2, giving option a.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7c959b9c517b17d9427de450def510b9673d91fd951e28696d4d56d8a768b74d.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(z),$ ${v}_{2}(z),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{2},\,\,0\le x\le {y}^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type II *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/c3837a3551b35a5146fd2c8e2441e4a9d6d947e8c52e44254d48eb854e54e605.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x={y}^{2}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{x}.
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
y=\sqrt{2}.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,\sqrt{x}\le y\le \sqrt{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/22581a56f4d9cb611bd9a58b06b1036cd47b500217570ae6890d0f38dba6742c.png)

We now consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the right curve given by 

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=\sqrt{x} \\ y=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\sqrt{x}=\sqrt{2}\,⟹\,x=2.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/e2305d3da63886703666fd58a2adfe8f15f2eceb7261922f46ba4949b0fc0cde.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ then $z,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{\sqrt{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

Question 7
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫02∫0y2f(x,y,z)dxdydz. so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then x, and then z. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∫01∫02∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
b
 ∫01∫0x∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
c
 ∫01∫02∫x2xf(x,y,z)dydxdz
d
 ∫01∫0x∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
e
 ∫01∫01∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We wish to find limits of integration u1(x,z), u2(x,z), v1(z), v2(z), a, and b such that

∫01∫02∫0y2f(x,y,z)dxdydz=∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dydxdz.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤2,0≤x≤y2}

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dydxdz, we write R as a type III region and its projection D onto the xz-plane as a type II plane region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the y-axis and in the direction of increasing y, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

  • The left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x,z), is x=y2⟹y=x.

  • The right boundary of the region is y=2.

Therefore, the type III representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,x≤y≤2},

as shown in the diagram below.

We now consider the projection D as a type II plane region in the xz-plane with the right curve given by

{y=xy=2⟹x=2⟹x=2.

Hence, we have that D={(x,z):0≤x≤2,0≤z≤1}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then x, then z, we obtain ∫01∫02∫0y2f(x,y,z)dxdydz=∫01∫02∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option a: x≤y² with y≥0 gives y≥√x, so the reordered bounds are 0≤z≤1, 0≤x≤2, and √x≤y≤√2. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option d.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration in a Triple Integral
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7c959b9c517b17d9427de450def510b9673d91fd951e28696d4d56d8a768b74d.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(z),$ ${v}_{2}(z),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{2},\,\,0\le x\le {y}^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type II *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/c3837a3551b35a5146fd2c8e2441e4a9d6d947e8c52e44254d48eb854e54e605.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x={y}^{2}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{x}.
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
y=\sqrt{2}.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,\sqrt{x}\le y\le \sqrt{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/22581a56f4d9cb611bd9a58b06b1036cd47b500217570ae6890d0f38dba6742c.png)

We now consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the right curve given by 

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=\sqrt{x} \\ y=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\sqrt{x}=\sqrt{2}\,⟹\,x=2.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/e2305d3da63886703666fd58a2adfe8f15f2eceb7261922f46ba4949b0fc0cde.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ then $z,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{\sqrt{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

Question 8
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫02x∫01−xf(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to x, then z, and then y. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∫02∫0y∫11−zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
b
 ∫02∫01−y/2∫11+zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
c
 ∫02∫01−y∫y/21−2zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
d
 ∫02∫01−y/2∫y/21−zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
e
 ∫02∫01−2y∫2y1−z/2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
Submit

decision.explanation: The constraints y≤2x and z≤1−x give y/2≤x≤1−z. This interval exists when 0≤z≤1−y/2, with 0≤y≤2. Therefore option d has the required order dx dz dy.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/192cb96645cef0340e99769af3126b9d7e3775ed419e8414e3ad1ed683e919e3.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z),$ ${u}_{2}(y,z),$ ${v}_{1}(y),$ ${v}_{2}(y),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2x,\,\,0\le z\le 1-x}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $R$ as a type II region and its projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $x$-axis and in the direction of increasing $x,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/60f61df1520d366f6cbcac0b87e7e5eb453e8f011ff046b29a61cdae41624ddf.png)

The arrow enters the region through the rear boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y,z),$ is

$$
z=1-x\,⟹\,x=1-z.
$$

- The rear boundary of the region is

$$
y=2x\,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le 1-z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/02bbf0de5dad7ff72970ef5a939ac66fd05dfc06c31a23c37b6204042e1859b8.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $yz$-plane with the top curve given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-z \\ x=\frac{y}{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\frac{y}{2}=1-z\,⟹\,z=1-\frac{y}{2}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2eea77ae3d1ae7a459dba98c98b20fabbec6b1d3a6cacb718b32688bd4ad11d7.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{y}{2}}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-y/2}{\int }_{y/2}^{1-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

Question 8
?

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫02x∫01−xf(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to x, then z, and then y. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∫02∫0y∫11−zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
b
 ∫02∫01−y/2∫11+zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
c
 ∫02∫01−y∫y/21−2zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
d
 ∫02∫01−y/2∫y/21−zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
e
 ∫02∫01−2y∫2y1−z/2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find limits of integration u1(y,z), u2(y,z), v1(y), v2(y), a, and b such that

∫01∫02x∫01−xf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdzdy.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤2x,0≤z≤1−x}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dxdzdy, we write R as a type II region and its projection D onto the yz-plane as a type I plane region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the x-axis and in the direction of increasing x, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the rear boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

  • The front boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y,z), is z=1−x⟹x=1−z.

  • The rear boundary of the region is y=2x⟹x=y2.

Therefore, the type II representation of R is R={(x,y,z):(y,z)∈D,y2≤x≤1−z}, as shown in the diagram below.

Now, we consider the projection D as a type I plane region in the yz-plane with the top curve given by {x=1−zx=y2⟹y2=1−z⟹z=1−y2.

Hence, we have that D={(y,z):0≤y≤2,0≤z≤1−y2}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to x, then z, and then y, we obtain

∫01∫02x∫01−xf(x,y,z)dzdydx=∫02∫01−y/2∫y/21−zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration in a Triple Integral
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/192cb96645cef0340e99769af3126b9d7e3775ed419e8414e3ad1ed683e919e3.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z),$ ${u}_{2}(y,z),$ ${v}_{1}(y),$ ${v}_{2}(y),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2x,\,\,0\le z\le 1-x}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $R$ as a type II region and its projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $x$-axis and in the direction of increasing $x,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/60f61df1520d366f6cbcac0b87e7e5eb453e8f011ff046b29a61cdae41624ddf.png)

The arrow enters the region through the rear boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y,z),$ is

$$
z=1-x\,⟹\,x=1-z.
$$

- The rear boundary of the region is

$$
y=2x\,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le 1-z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/02bbf0de5dad7ff72970ef5a939ac66fd05dfc06c31a23c37b6204042e1859b8.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $yz$-plane with the top curve given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-z \\ x=\frac{y}{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\frac{y}{2}=1-z\,⟹\,z=1-\frac{y}{2}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2eea77ae3d1ae7a459dba98c98b20fabbec6b1d3a6cacb718b32688bd4ad11d7.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{y}{2}}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-y/2}{\int }_{y/2}^{1-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

c

decision.explanation: The region satisfies 0≤x≤∛2 and 0≤y³≤z≤2. For fixed z, this gives 0≤y≤∛z, while 0≤z≤2. Thus option d gives the required order dy dz dx.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Change the order of integration in the following integral, 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ then $x.$
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 2}
$$

Now, let's sketch the region. Since it is a type I region, we first sketch the projection onto the $xy$-plane, given by

$$
E={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{2}}.
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/58a9056015b3dad91ec7ae64bff893c8c6c2cce6480c979545e423cbe105ef03.png)

Then, the region $R$ is shown in the diagram below, where ${y}^{3}\le z\le 2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2fdd6a15b4ddadfc3ee24af5e35e2a87e9e963ceeefbf858b704d78ee0b78513.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/65da730d32f200b8f9da004ee8cf6b7e79095e323961f4a5b6dfa0bddeace42b.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=(x,z),$ is

$$
z={y}^{3}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt[3]{z}
$$

- The left boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/1743f540a85fc1c266c84da8f34b2012516b7bbc98d113cf7c62ba3bba8173c1.png)

We now consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the top curve given by 

$$
z=(\sqrt[3]{2})^{3}=2.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/b76bf84e1179bec6a1e8e357c6cc628eee95c1663e6f0ff375135612a6f275de.png)

Hence,

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le z\le 2}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}f(x,y,z)\,\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

c

EXPLANATION

We wish to find limits of integration u1(x,z), u2(x,z), v1(x), v2(x), a, and b such that

∫023∫023∫y32f(x,y,z)dzdydx=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dydzdx.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤23,0≤y≤23,y3≤z≤2}

Now, let's sketch the region. Since it is a type I region, we first sketch the projection onto the xy-plane, given by E={(x,y):0≤x≤23,0≤y≤23}.

as shown below.

Then, the region R is shown in the diagram below, where y3≤z≤2.

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dydzdx, we write R as a type III region and its projection D onto the xz-plane as a type I plane region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the y-axis and in the direction of increasing y, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

  • The right boundary of the region, written in the form y=(x,z), is z=y3⟹y=z3

  • The left boundary of the region is y=0.

Therefore, the type III representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,0≤y≤z3},

as shown in the diagram below.

We now consider the projection D as a type II plane region in the xz-plane with the top curve given by

z=(23)3=2.

Hence, D={(x,z):0≤x≤23,0≤z≤2}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∫023∫023∫y32f(x,y,z)dzdydx=∫023∫02∫0z3f(x,y,z)dydzdx.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration in a Triple Integral
content.problem:
Change the order of integration in the following integral, 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ then $x.$
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 2}
$$

Now, let's sketch the region. Since it is a type I region, we first sketch the projection onto the $xy$-plane, given by

$$
E={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{2}}.
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/58a9056015b3dad91ec7ae64bff893c8c6c2cce6480c979545e423cbe105ef03.png)

Then, the region $R$ is shown in the diagram below, where ${y}^{3}\le z\le 2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2fdd6a15b4ddadfc3ee24af5e35e2a87e9e963ceeefbf858b704d78ee0b78513.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/65da730d32f200b8f9da004ee8cf6b7e79095e323961f4a5b6dfa0bddeace42b.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=(x,z),$ is

$$
z={y}^{3}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt[3]{z}
$$

- The left boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/1743f540a85fc1c266c84da8f34b2012516b7bbc98d113cf7c62ba3bba8173c1.png)

We now consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the top curve given by 

$$
z=(\sqrt[3]{2})^{3}=2.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/b76bf84e1179bec6a1e8e357c6cc628eee95c1663e6f0ff375135612a6f275de.png)

Hence,

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{2},\,\,0\le z\le 2}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}f(x,y,z)\,\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$
